cards.subject: Every floor below the top one
lines: Patch 4.0.3a removed all of them, and every boss standing on them — Atal'alarion, the statue circle, the whole descent.
This is the only place the temple is still the shape it was built.

cards.subject: The hole
cards.tag: In the middle of the upper pit
lines: There is an open drop, and the fall kills anyone without slow fall or levitate.
It is not a shortcut.
It is the single most reliable way to lose a group member in this building.

cards.subject: Two circles, and they are not the same six
lines: Six statues ring the Pit of Refuse in the basement, and they are a sequence lock.
Six Atal'ai Defenders stand on ledges over the Pit of Sacrifice, and killing all six drops Jammal'an's shield.
Two pits, two puzzles. Almost everybody remembers them as one.

cards.subject: The order is kept in Tanaris
cards.tag: S, N, SW, SE, NW, NE
lines: Nothing inside the temple tells you.
It comes from a dwarf archaeologist out in the sand who noticed the lights and sent somebody to try them.
Then you use the altar.

cards.subject: Something was waiting down there
lines: Atal'alarion rises — a dire troll, sworn protector of the idol on the lowest level.
"My banishment has ended, let the blood flow!"
Banished. Somebody put him under there on purpose, and you have just let him out.

cards.subject: The dragons are the recipe
lines: Jammal'an's meditations told him to bring Hakkar back using the blood of green dragons.
Those four are Eranikus's own retinue, and the pit they live in is a larder.
The guards and the ritual component are the same animals.

cards.subject: Why there is a dungeon at all
lines: Ysera left green dragons over the sunken ruin. The Emerald Nightmare took them — Eranikus among the first dragons ever to fall to it.
Only once the watchmen were corrupted did the Atal'ai walk back into their own temple.
The failure of the guard is the reason there is anything in here.

cards.subject: Ogom the Wretched
lines: Jammal'an does not stand alone in the pew room.
The high priest of a god of blood keeps a corpse to protect him.

cards.subject: He was half right
lines: His prophecy was that summoning Hakkar would buy the tribe immortality. He was wrong about that.
He dies saying "Ya not be gettin' me dat easy! Atal'ai gonna rise up..."
The rising up did happen. Further south, and later.

cards.subject: You are the one who summons Hakkar
lines: The Avatar is not a boss the dungeon leads to. You carry an egg in from Tanaris, kill the bloodrinkers, use their blood to put out the eternal flames, and call him up yourself.
A thousand years of Atal'ai failed at this. You do it on a fetch quest.
Then you catch his essence in the same egg and hand it in.

cards.subject: The Shade is not the dragon
lines: He is described as pulled between the Emerald Dream and the physical world. The real Eranikus is elsewhere, and unreachable, for all of this game.
You cannot kill him here.
You kill the part of him that leaked through.

cards.subject: What he shouts at you
cards.tag: It is not a villain's line
lines: "This evil cannot be allowed to enter this world! Come my children!"
Ysera posted him here to stop Hakkar.
Mad, corrupted, thousands of years in, he is still saying the words of the job — at the people who came to do it.
